t: The war began from a dispute over Article 17 of the Treaty of Wuchale, which the Italian text read as making Ethiopia a protectorate of Italy and the Amharic text read as an offer of Italy's good offices.
Baratieri attacked under pressure from Rome and from his own generals, and his columns, advancing on poor maps, lost touch with one another and were defeated one after another.
Prisoners were treated unequally: about 800 captured Eritrean askari were mutilated, and around 70 Italian prisoners were massacred in retaliation for the death of Bashah Aboye.
dyk: The Italian army at Adwa consisted mainly of white European troops, unlike most European armies of the Scramble for Africa, and the newer Carcano Model 91 rifles were not issued according to Chris Prouty, because Baratieri was under constraints to be economical and wanted to use up the old cartridges.
ev: Italy and King Menelik of Shewa sign the Treaty of Wuchale, whose Italian and Amharic versions of Article 17 differ
Baratieri defeats Ras Mengesha Yohannes at Coatit in January, and Menelik issues a call to arms to the whole population in September
An Ethiopian vanguard destroys a small Italian unit at Amba Alagi on 7 December, and the Italians withdraw to more defensible positions in Tigray
On 29 February Baratieri meets his generals, who argue for an attack rather than a retreat
The Italian columns advance after midnight and the battle is fought on 1 March, ending in the collapse of all four brigades
Baratieri reaches Adi Keyh on 2 March and telegraphs news of the defeat to Rome
Prime Minister Crispi resigns on 9 March, and Italy later signs the Treaty of Addis Ababa
Italy launches the Second Italo-Ethiopian War on 3 October, and Ethiopian forces are defeated by May 1936

f.place: Near the town of Adwa, in the Tigray region of northern Ethiopia, on the mountains and in the valleys west and south of the town
f.sides: The Ethiopian Empire under Emperor Menelik II, with estimates of between 73,000 and over 100,000 men; an Italian colonial force under General Oreste Baratieri, estimated at 14,519 effective combat troops by Harold Marcus and at 17,770 with fifty-six artillery pieces by David Levering Lewis
f.outcome: An Ethiopian victory: over 6,000 Italian and colonial troops were killed and around 3,800 captured, by one set of figures. Italy later signed the Treaty of Addis Ababa, recognising Ethiopia as independent.
